newsitem.title: ISRAEL: U.S. investor group eyes Hapoalim stake.
newsitem.headline: U.S. investor group eyes Hapoalim stake.

text.p: Investors led by Jeffrey Keil, outgoing president of Republic New York Corp, have expressed interest in bidding for a stake in Israel's largest bank, Bank Hapoalim, a senior Israeli Treasury official said.
"He has shown some interest," David Brodett, director general of the Treasury, told Reuters on Tuesday.

Keil announced in June he would leave his post at Republic on September 30 to form his own investment partnership. At the time it was reported that Keil would invest in Israel's financial sector, with Republic possibly acting as a partner.

Brodett said other investors have also expressed interest since a consortium led by Claridge Israel dropped out of the bidding for Hapoalim last month. Claridge is the Israeli investment vehicle of Canadian businessman Charles Bronfman. The group included Ted Arison of Carnival Corp and Goldman Sachs.
Another group led by Israeli businessman Eliezer Fishman and which includes Bear Stearns has yet to receive approval from the central Bank of Israel to bid.
Brodett said the government was going ahead with its plan to sell a controlling stake in Israel's largest bank but he could not say whether a new tender would be issued.

Sources in the prime minister's office have said the prime minister's office favoured privatising the state banks by offering shares on the bourse rather than by selling controlling stakes to strategic investors.
According to the Globes financial newspaper, Keil has set up a $500 million investment partnership in the United States.
Republic New York is controlled by financier Edmond Safra, who was the sole bidder for a stake in Bank Leumi, Israel's second-largest bank, until he withdrew his bid last year.
Safra's brothers control the First International Bank of Israel.
Globes said it was not clear whether the Safra family was involved in Keil's partnership.
